NoteTexAccessor::deaccent¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::deaccent() const

Remove Authored Accent Marks Without Removing Text¶

deaccent() converts accented text to its unaccented form in two representations: TeX accent commands are unwrapped to their operand, and accented UTF-8 Latin characters are transliterated to their base character. It is intended for search keys, comparison text, and other workflows where accent distinctions should not separate otherwise equivalent words.

The recognized TeX control-symbol accents are \', \", \` , \^, \~, \=, and \.. The recognized control-word accents are \v, \u, \H, \c, \k, \b, \d, \r, and \t. An operand may be braced or a single following UTF-8 code point; spaces after a control-word accent are syntax separators and are not retained. A balanced braced operand is retained in full, so \t{oo} becomes oo rather than losing one character.

Matching is exact. An ordinary command such as \text{keep} is not treated as the \t accent, unknown commands remain unchanged, and a doubled backslash is an escaped command boundary. This distinction prevents accent cleanup from silently damaging unrelated TeX source. The operation does not transliterate general scripts, remove punctuation, or erase arbitrary combining syntax.

The operation is lane-wise, out-of-place, and shape preserving. It allocates a new Text Note and leaves the receiver unchanged. Empty cells remain empty; undefined input remains undefined; all defined non-Text dtypes are rejected. The scanner is linear in source bytes and writes directly into one result string per cell before packing those strings into the output arena.

Example 1: TeX Accent Forms And Command Boundaries¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\'{e} \v S \c{c} \t{oo} \text{keep})",
                             "caf\xC3\xA9 d\xC3\xA9j\xC3\xA0",
                             R"(\\'{e} \unknown{x})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});

std::cout << source.tex().deaccent() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["e S c oo \\text{keep}", "cafe deja"],
  ["\\\\'{e} \\unknown{x}", ""]
]

Braced, unbraced, control-symbol, and control-word accents are unwrapped. The ordinary, escaped, and unknown commands remain byte-for-byte intact.

Example 2: Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto plain = source.tex().deaccent();
std::cout << "shape=[" << plain.sizes()[0] << ", " << plain.sizes()[1]
          << "] dtype=" << pluss::coden::dtype_name(plain.dtype()) << '\n';

Output¶

shape=[2, 2] dtype=Text

Example 3: The Receiver Is Not Mutated¶

const auto original = pluss::make_note(R"(\'{e})");
const auto plain = original.tex().deaccent();
std::cout << original << '\n' << plain << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"\\'{e}"
Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"e"

Example 4: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().deaccent().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().deaccent();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "deaccent Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
deaccent Int64: rejected
